operational-example.copy: Use Motion Boundary as a bounded component: Wrap one region with explicit enter, exit, active, and reduced-motion behavior without choreographing the whole page.

scenario.title: Motion Boundary
scenario.meta: Bounded enter, active, and exit motion
rationale: Motion Boundary wraps one region and exposes idle, entering, active, exiting, reduced-motion, and disabled states without choreographing the page.
Entering uses Flow enter duration/easing; exiting uses Flow exit duration/easing; active uses move easing for continuity.
Route/page choreography, storytelling, and multi-region sequencing belong to patterns or foundations, not this component.

rows.label: Entering
rows.value: Uses Flow enter duration and easing.

rows.label: Exiting
rows.value: Uses Flow exit duration and easing.

rows.label: Boundary
rows.value: One bounded region only; choreography escalates.

items.rule: Owns the visible Motion Boundary container and spacing.
Provides visible meaning and accessible name.
Shows idle, entering, active, exiting, reduced-motion, and disabled states with separate enter, move, and exit timing tokens.
Keeps context short and local to the component.
Uses a bounded cue to reveal transition direction and progress without becoming page choreography.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, reduced-motion, exiting, entering, active, idle
items: Expose current state through text or ARIA where applicable.
Keep keyboard focus visible and predictable.
Respect reduced motion for motion-bearing variants.
Escalate to a pattern when behavior exceeds one local component.

variants.copy: Motion Boundary variants define local presentation only. Fade, slide, collapse, and route change the cue treatment; they do not own page choreography or route transition systems.

states.copy: Motion Boundary states follow explicit precedence: disabled, reduced-motion, exiting, entering, active, idle. Entering uses Flow enter timing, exiting uses Flow exit timing, and active uses move timing.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant controls presentation; state controls local behavior. Page choreography, route transition systems, and animation storytelling belong to patterns or foundations.

full-width.copy: Motion Boundary may fill its parent when content remains readable and behavior stays local.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use responsive density to preserve labels, state, and targets; do not add pattern orchestration to Motion Boundary.

viewport-organization.copy: Viewport rules decide density and placement while Motion Boundary remains a component.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use readable labels and touch-safe targets.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep the component near related context.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact density only when state remains visible.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify Motion Boundary label, variant, state, full-width behavior, and pattern boundary.

api-foundations.copy: Motion Boundary API exposes local props while Design System owns foundations, primitives, state precedence, and escalation rules.

props.name: description
props.notes: Short description for the bounded region.

groups.title: Use
items: Use Motion Boundary for one bounded component job.
Keep label, state, and context visible.
Use Design System tokens and accessibility rules.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Page choreography, route transition systems, and animation storytelling belong to patterns or foundations.
Do not hide required meaning in icons, color, or animation only.
Do not add process orchestration inside the component.

groups.title: Review
items: Check enter, active, exit, reduced-motion, and disabled states.
Confirm entering uses Flow enter timing and exiting uses Flow exit timing.
Escalate page choreography, route transition systems, and animation storytelling to patterns or foundations.

rejectIf: Page choreography, route transition systems, and animation storytelling belong to patterns or foundations.
Entering and exiting use the same undocumented timing.
Required label or fallback is missing.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Motion Boundary as a bounded component. Agents may place it when the job is local; humans confirm state, accessibility, content, and whether escalation to a pattern is required.
canDecide: Use Motion Boundary for one local UI job.
Select variant and state from the Motion Boundary contract.
Keep labels, focus, and state visible.
mustAsk: The request needs orchestration, multi-step behavior, or cross-surface state.
Page choreography, route transition systems, and animation storytelling belong to patterns or foundations.
Accessibility, risk, or reduced-motion expectations are unclear.
rejectIf: Page choreography, route transition systems, and animation storytelling belong to patterns or foundations.
Required meaning is icon-only, color-only, or motion-only.
The component becomes a process container.
miel.handoff: I am using Motion Boundary as a bounded component. Please confirm label, state, accessibility behavior, responsive treatment, and whether this should escalate to a pattern.
